author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Rhode Island Blood Center is using Childhood Cancer Awareness Month to remind residents that transfusions are a routine and often urgent part of treatment for many young cancer patients.

More than 15,000 children and adolescents are diagnosed with cancer in the United States each year, the center said. Chemotherapy, surgery and complications from treatment can create a need for red cells, platelets or plasma. The center estimates that more than 60% of people are eligible to donate blood, while only about 3% do so.

NBC 10 highlighted the family of Carrigan Nelson, who was diagnosed with osteosarcoma shortly after her 18th birthday. Her family said blood products helped extend her life during seven years of treatment before her death in 2025. They are encouraging eligible donors to give in her memory and for other patients.

A community back-to-school blood drive is scheduled for Monday, September 14, from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. at the Crowne Plaza in Warwick. Donor eligibility and appointment details are available from the Rhode Island Blood Center.
dek: The center says many young cancer patients depend on blood components and is promoting a September 14 community drive in Warwick.
headline: Rhode Island Blood Center urges donors during childhood cancer campaign
